name: FHFA House Price Index (HPI) — state/MSA quarterly, county annual
proposed_use: A second, independent national appreciation series to cross-check and extend Zillow ZHVI (zillow_research.py) — especially valuable once the screener generalizes past NYC, since Zillow's condo-tier ZHVI thins out in smaller metros while FHFA HPI covers every state and most MSAs/counties. Also a natural ground-truth series for backtest.py and for the 'FHFA tract HPI growth' benchmark the research-sources skill itself names as an evaluation target.
coverage: national (all states; most MSAs; counties via the annual 'Developmental Index')
granularity: state and MSA quarterly; county annual (not tract — the skill's mention of 'tract HPI' is aspirational/inaccurate, FHFA's finest published geography is county)
history_start: 1975 (state); varies by MSA/county, many back to the 1980s-90s
license: US government work, public domain. Master CSV is openly downloadable with no API key and no login.
cost: Free, no key, no rate limit beyond ordinary fair-use HTTP fetching of a static file.
api_key_notes: None needed — simplest ingestion of any candidate here, just a scheduled CSV pull.
rate_limit: None published; it's a static file download.
recommendation: Strong recommend, and the easiest to ship of the four candidates here: zero credentials, zero rate-limit logic, a single master CSV (https://www.fhfa.gov/hpi/download/monthly/hpi_master.csv per FHFA's datasets page). The catch is geographic granularity — county-level is annual only, not quarterly, so it complements rather than replaces Zillow ZHVI's monthly ZIP-level series for NYC itself. Its real value is generalization: when this screener is pointed at a metro where Zillow's condo-tier series is thin or absent, FHFA HPI is the one series guaranteed to exist for that county. Worth implementing specifically to de-risk the multi-market expansion, not to improve NYC accuracy.
